Seven tries (Lakai, Vaa'i, Roigard, Taylor, Carter, Moorby, Jordan) and 15 points from Damian McKenzie retained the Bledisloe Cup for a 24th straight year and stretched the Eden Park unbeaten run to 54.
Black Ferns scored 13 tries, including four to Shyrah Tuliau-Tua'a, to lead 43-0 at halftime and take a 1-0 series lead over a weakened France.
Six first-half tries had the All Blacks 36-7 up at the break, capped by Beauden Barrett's 70m intercept try; Josh Moorby and Barrett both scored twice for a 13th straight Bledisloe win.

news.title: Dubois stops Wardley in round two to keep WBO heavyweight belt
news.summary: Daniel Dubois dropped Fabio Wardley in the first and forced the towel in the second at The O2. Wardley beat Joseph Parker at the same venue in October 2025.

news.title: Parker rematch floated as an option for Wardley after Dubois defeat
news.summary: With Parker cleared to return, a rematch with Wardley is named as a possible next step, along with Jarrell Miller and Lawrence Okolie. No fight is confirmed.

news.title: Fundora retains WBC 154lb title with last-second KO
news.summary: Sebastian Fundora knocked out Ermal Hadribeaj at 2:59 of round 12 in Las Vegas.

news.title: Figueroa stripped after missing weight, Kameda title fight cancelled
news.summary: Brandon Figueroa lost his WBA featherweight title on the scales, and his bout with Tomoki Kameda was cancelled.

news.title: Itauma lined up for January comeback
news.summary: Frank Warren says Moses Itauma will fight in January against a testing opponent, possibly one win from another world title shot. No date or opponent has been named yet.

news.title: Canelo v Mbilli to go ahead despite Riyadh attacks
news.summary: Turki Alalshikh says the 31 October WBC super-middleweight fight will go ahead despite deadly strikes on Riyadh, and Canelo has agreed to proceed.

news.title: Bivol to defend titles against Callum Smith in Yekaterinburg
news.summary: Dmitry Bivol will defend his WBA, IBF and WBO light-heavyweight titles against Callum Smith at the UMMC Arena on 12 December.

news.title: Mendoza stuns Sandoval to become unified flyweight champion
news.summary: Sergio Mendoza scored three knockdowns to stop Ricardo Sandoval in round five in Chicago. Earlier on the card, Floyd Schofield won the vacant WBA lightweight title.

news.title: Rose Bowl to be contested in T20I series
news.summary: The Rose Bowl will now be on the line in all White Ferns v Australia white-ball series, starting with the three T20Is in Sydney this week. All three are live on Sky Sport in NZ.

news.title: White Ferns lose rain-hit warm-up to Governor-General's XI
news.summary: The GG's XI won by 19 runs on DLS at North Sydney Oval, with Lucy Finn taking 3-5; Bella James hit 31 not out off 13.

news.title: Free fan launch for India series in Christchurch
news.summary: The T20I squad will be at Victoria Square on Wednesday 21 October from 4pm, the eve of the 8pm series opener at Hagley Oval.

news.title: Super Smash schedule released
news.summary: The Super Smash starts 27 December with doubleheaders in Auckland, Palmerston North and Alexandra, and finals in Auckland on 28-30 January. 24 games are free on TVNZ+ and DUKE, and the rest stream on NZC's YouTube.

news.title: O'Rourke to miss India tour
news.summary: Will O'Rourke is skipping the India series as a precaution with hamstring and calf injuries. He is targeting a return for Canterbury in late November and the Perth Test on 9 December.

news.title: ODI squads named: Allen, Ferguson and Seifert back, Ravindra returns
news.summary: Santner captains split squads for the five ODIs against India. Allen, Ferguson and Seifert join for games 4 and 5 while Test players head to Wellington.

news.title: Chapman and Foulkes ruled out of India T20Is
news.summary: Mark Chapman (torn hamstring) and Zak Foulkes (hip flexor) are out of the T20Is, and Josh Clarkson and Blair Tickner have been called in.

news.title: Jeet Raval retires
news.summary: The 24-Test opener retires after more than 10,000 first-class runs for Auckland, Central Stags and Northern Districts.

news.title: BJ Watling named Black Caps batting coach
news.summary: Watling joins on 16 November and takes over from Luke Ronchi before the four-Test tour of Australia.

news.title: Adams and Guptill join White Ferns coaching group
news.summary: Andre Adams and Martin Guptill join interim coach Dean Brownlie for the Australia T20Is. Guptill is covering for Craig McMillan, who is recovering from back surgery.

news.title: NZC Board explains NZ20 choice
news.summary: The Board voted 7-0 for a six-team NZ20 T20 competition, planned to launch in 2027-28.

news.title: Ed Nuttall steps away from cricket
news.summary: The Canterbury left-arm quick, who took 134 first-class wickets, is retiring before the season to work in insurance.

news.title: Bracewell goes casual, Kelly earns first central contract
news.summary: Michael Bracewell switches to a casual contract to chase a Big Bash League deal. Northern Districts batter Nick Kelly, 33, takes his central contract spot.

news.title: Carson, Penfold, James and Rowe recalled for Australia T20Is
news.summary: Melie Kerr leads a 15-player squad with Dean Brownlie as interim head coach. Izzy Gaze is out after thumb surgery.

news.title: Milne returns for India T20Is, Ravindra ruled out
news.summary: Adam Milne and Michael Bracewell return from injury in Santner's 16-man squad, while Rachin Ravindra misses the T20Is with a dislocated shoulder.

news.title: Ponga breaks arm in World Cup opener
news.summary: Kalyn Ponga fractured the radius in his left arm against Australia and was booked for surgery. He stays in camp, and Keano Kini is likely to start at fullback against the Cook Islands.

news.title: Brave Ponga racing the clock; McLean shoulder not serious
news.summary: Teammates hope Ponga could be back by the 15 November final. Coach Stacey Jones says Casey McLean's shoulder injury is not serious.

news.title: Kangaroos edge Kiwis 24-22 in World Cup opener
news.summary: Jack Bostock's debut hat-trick and a late winning try gave Australia victory in Sydney in front of a record 41,255 crowd.

news.title: Ponga and Gagai among new faces in Kiwis World Cup squad
news.summary: Stacey Jones named 23 players, captained by James Fisher-Harris. The six Warriors are Fisher-Harris, Erin Clark, Jacob Laban, Te Maire Martin, Charnze Nicoll-Klokstad and Tanner Stowers-Smith.

news.title: Olympic sevens duo bolster Kiwi Ferns World Cup squad
news.summary: Ricky Henry named 23 players, with seven potential debutants including Olympic gold medallists Stacey Waaka and Tenika Willison. Raecene McGregor and Georgia Hale are co-captains.

news.title: Five Warriors women in Kiwi Ferns squad
news.summary: Kaiyah Atai, Mele Hufanga, Ivana Lauitiiti, Apii Nicholls and Stacey Waaka of the Warriors NRLW side are in the Kiwi Ferns World Cup squad.

news.title: Rocco Berry re-signs with Warriors for 2027
news.summary: The centre missed the 2026 NRL season through injury and has signed a one-year deal. He has played 52 games and scored 13 tries for the club.

news.title: Webster named NRL Coach of the Year
news.summary: Andrew Webster won Coach of the Year at the Dally M awards after guiding the Warriors to second on the ladder. Finals were not counted in the voting.

news.title: Knights end Warriors' season at a record-crowd Eden Park
news.summary: The Warriors lost 12-10 to Newcastle in front of more than 48,000, after a 26-16 qualifying-final loss to the Dolphins. That ended a season in which they finished second on the ladder.

news.title: Kiwi Ferns open World Cup against Fiji today
news.summary: The Kiwi Ferns begin their Group B campaign against Fiji Bulikula at McDonald Jones Stadium, Newcastle, at 3:50pm NZT, live on Sky Sport Now.

news.title: Northland beat Otago to reach the NPC final
news.summary: Northland beat Otago 38-19 in Whangarei, with Rivez Reihana scoring two tries and 18 points. They will face the Canterbury v Taranaki winner.

news.title: Taranaki's run of 50-point wins sets up Canterbury semi
news.summary: Taranaki became the first NPC side to win four straight games by 50-plus points, and Jacob Ratumaitavuki-Kneepkens says the squad is peaking. Canterbury beat Waikato 62-26 for their sixth win in a row.

news.title: The top performers from the NPC quarter-finals
news.summary: A look back at the quarter-finals. Taranaki, Canterbury, Otago and Northland went through, and Taranaki beat North Harbour 50-31.

news.title: NPC crowds up 57 per cent in 50th season
news.summary: Regular-season crowds rose 57% to more than 300,000, and social media views rose 103%. The season produced 645 tries at an average of 61.6 points a game.

news.title: Counties Manukau retain the Ranfurly Shield against Hawke's Bay
news.summary: Counties won a tight first defence 12-7 at home in Pukekohe to hold the Shield through the off-season.

news.title: Late penalty sees Counties stun Northland to win the Ranfurly Shield
news.summary: Counties Manukau won 22-19 in Whangarei with a 79th-minute penalty to take the Shield from Northland.

news.title: Canterbury v Auckland and Wellington v Northland in FPC finals
news.summary: Canterbury beat Manawatu 57-7 and Auckland Storm beat Waikato 36-31 to set up the Premiership final. Wellington beat Hawke's Bay Tui 51-26 to reach the Championship final.

news.title: Canterbury beat Auckland Storm 50-24 in the FPC Premiership final
news.summary: Canterbury beat Auckland Storm 50-24 in the final at One NZ Stadium. A day earlier, Wellington Pride beat Northland 39-15 in the Championship final.

news.title: Ardie Savea joins the Blues for 2027
news.summary: The All Blacks captain has signed a one-year deal with the Blues after Moana Pasifika's exit. He is recovering from shoulder surgery.

news.title: Hurricanes sign six-time champion Bryn Hall
news.summary: Former Crusaders halfback Bryn Hall has joined the Hurricanes on a one-year deal to back up Cameron Roigard in their title defence.

news.title: Frizell and Scott Barrett back in 34-man Bledisloe squad
news.summary: Codie Taylor captains a 34-man squad with Ardie Savea (shoulder) out; Shannon Frizell earns his first selection since the 2023 World Cup final and Scott Barrett returns from back surgery, while Noah Hotham misses out.

news.title: Mo'unga tears calf as Rennie calls it his hardest team to pick
news.summary: Richie Mo'unga was named at 10 then tore a calf at training and misses the Bledisloe series, with Damian McKenzie stepping in; Fehi Fineanganofo is also out and Ruben Love is done for the year.

news.title: All Blacks rout Wallabies 50-19 to retain Bledisloe Cup
news.summary: A five-try second-half surge at Eden Park kept the Bledisloe Cup in New Zealand for a 24th consecutive year.

news.title: Eight changes for Sydney as Jordie Barrett ruled out
news.summary: Leroy Carter's ankle injury promoted Josh Moorby to start, Fabian Holland joined Scott Barrett at lock, and Jordie Barrett was later withdrawn with a tight calf.

news.title: All Blacks beat Wallabies 43-21 in Sydney
news.summary: A 36-7 halftime lead set up a 13th straight Bledisloe win; Quinn Tupaea failed an HIA and Chay Fihaki was sin-binned for a head-on-head tackle late on.

news.title: Black Ferns stay unbeaten with 66-14 win over Scotland
news.summary: New Zealand led 38-14 at halftime in Edinburgh, though Scotland scored their first ever tries against the Black Ferns.

news.title: England edge Black Ferns 26-19 with last-gasp intercept
news.summary: Zoe Harrison's interception try after the hooter at Twickenham, in front of nearly 60,000, ended Whitney Hansen's unbeaten start as coach.

news.title: Hansen relishing home support for France series
news.summary: Whitney Hansen said selection for the first France Test was a long, tough meeting and starting spots are not locked in, as the side looks to bounce back from the England loss.

news.title: France bring four debutants to Hamilton
news.summary: France named four uncapped players and handed Alexandra Chambon the captaincy, with Manae Feleu and Pauline Bourdon Sansus unavailable.

news.title: Black Ferns score 13 tries in 81-12 rout of France
news.summary: Shyrah Tuliau-Tua'a scored four tries and Ayesha Leti-I'iga made four linebreaks as New Zealand went 1-0 up in the three-Test series; game two is in Whangārei next Saturday.
